probes.question: True or false: in the classic data, low performers rated themselves higher than high performers did.
What does the statistical explanation say about the effect?
options: It may largely be a mere statistical effect
It proves poor performers cannot learn

image.alt: A simple line chart with confidence on the vertical axis and competence on the horizontal axis, showing a sharp early peak, a deep dip, then a slow rise.

body.claim: The Dunning-Kruger effect does not show that unskilled people rate themselves above experts.
body.why: In the classic exam data, low performers overestimated their abilities, but their self-assessment was still lower than that of high performers. Laypeople often misread it as saying low-intelligence people are more confident than high-intelligence people. Some critics argue the pattern may largely be a statistical effect, plus a general tendency to think we are better than average.
